frontend: mGBA 0.10.5 (the macOS app, mGBA.app), isolated config (XDG_CONFIG_HOME)

rom.name: Legend of Zelda, The - The Minish Cap (USA).gba

script: scripts/gba/Legend of Zelda, The - The Minish Cap.txt
input: none in the app: it was started with -t STATE and left running ~25 s, then sent SIGTERM. The game's own save routine ran inside the app and the app wrote the file.
started_from: save state of the libretro mgba core (0.11-212-7a12d6d) under tools/retro-run, taken 2 frames after script line 20 (the press that starts the game's save), with battery RAM dumped at the same moment and placed beside the ROM as the app's .sav. Its version word was lowered from 0x0100000B (0.11) to 0x01000007, the newest mGBA 0.10.5 accepts; it loaded with only a BIOS-checksum warning.

layout.save_dir: beside the ROM (the app default: savegamePath unset)
layout.name: <ROM file name without extension>.sav
layout.clock: appended to the .sav, no sidecar: GBA 16 bytes (7 BCD time bytes YY MM DD WD hh mm ss, control, u64 lastLatch); GB MBC3 48 bytes (the VBA-M layout libretro mgba writes as .rtc)
layout.written: while the game runs (the .sav is a mapped file), not only on exit

note: proof.png is the libretro mgba core booting with this file as its .srm (screen capture of the app is not permitted here): the game lists the save. EEPROM 8 KiB, no footer. The game writes the EEPROM over ~100 frames after END is chosen; in the app it did so with no input. Byte-identical to what libretro mgba holds at the same point of the script (27b1030f...).
